If I were the regional manager, I would restructure the renewal process.

Rosa, did you get the same request from the director's office? One page, informal, what would you change if the decision were yours.
I did. And the informal part is the difficult part. If he asked for a formal report, I would know exactly what to write.
That is the whole point, I think. He does not want the consultant version.
So what is yours? What would you change?
One thing. If I were in charge, I would give every account manager a real budget for retention. Right now, if a competitor calls my client, I have nothing to offer except a phone call.
That is a good one. In your position I would probably start somewhere else, though. If we streamlined the renewal approval, half of those calls would never happen.
Say that exactly like that on your page. Not the version with an executive summary. That version.
Then send me yours before the end of the month and I will send you mine. If we read each other's first, neither of us would write something safe.
If I were in charge, I would start with the renewal process.
If we lost that account, our market share would drop.
I would rather push back on the date than promise something we cannot do.

Rosa, it is Beatriz from the regional director's office. He is preparing the strategy session for December and he has asked four account managers for something unusual. Not a report. One page, informal, answering a single question: what would you change if the decision were yours? He is serious about the informal part. He said, and I am quoting him, that if he wanted a formal document he would ask the consultants, and that he already knows what the consultants would say. He wants the version you would tell a colleague in the corridor. One page, by the end of the month. And if you would rather talk it through instead of writing it, call me and we will book twenty minutes with him.

Here is the thing about strategy that nobody says out loud in the meeting. Most people in this industry know exactly what they would change. Ask any account manager what they would do if they ran the commercial area, and you will get a clear, specific, sensible answer in about fifteen seconds. Ask the same person to write it in a document that goes upstairs and it takes three weeks and comes back as nothing. The problem is not the idea. The problem is that we treat the strategy conversation as if it needed a special language. It does not. If I could change one thing about how this company plans, I would ask people the question in the corridor and write down what they actually say.
